dataset.name: SPRUCE S1 Bog Vegetation Survey and Peat Depth Data: 2009
description: This data set reports the results of a field survey of the S1 Bog to characterize the vegetation and to determine peat depth. The survey was conducted on September 21 and 22, 2009. This initial survey of vegetation and peat depth characteristics of the target bog was conducted to evaluate the logical locations for installing replicated experimental blocks for SPRUCE. The goal was to identify multiple locations of uniform aboveground vegetation and belowground peat depth for positioning experimental units within the bog. The experimental work was conducted in a Picea mariana [black spruce] - Sphagnum spp. bog forest in northern Minnesota, 40 km north of Grand Rapids, in the USDA Forest Service Marcell Experimental Forest (MEF). There is one (*.csv) data file containing the vegetation survey data and observations, and the peat depth measurements. Also included are figures of the spatial distributions of vegetation survey and peat depth results (Vegetation_survey_2009_figures.pdf). Photos of the surveyed plots are included in several *.zip files.photos.

measurementTechnique:
Overview:
On the 21 and 22 September 2009 ORNL and U.S. Forest Service staff surveyed the areal extent of the S1 Bog for vegetation and peat characteristics.
The bog vegetation was surveyed through direct measurements of 165 plots distributed on a 20 meter spacing along 30 northwest-to-southeast transects (Figure 2.). Tree species, number, diameter at 1.3 meters (DBH), and total height were evaluated within a 2.5 meter radius of the plot center. Seedling/sapling species and count were evaluated within a 1 m radius of the plot center. A semi-quantitative visual estimation of the cover of the dominant ericaceous shrub cover was made within a 1-m subplot. Notes were taken regarding the condition of the Sphagnum layer, the presence of other common forms of ground vegetation, and the occurrence of buried logs within the peat. Photographs of the plots were taken.
The thickness of peat was measured directly with manual push probes. Triplicate measurements were made at most of the 165 plots using 0.5 cm diameter metal rods.

Site Description:
The site is the 8.1-ha S1 bog, a Picea mariana [black spruce] – Sphagnum spp. ombrotrophic bog forest in northern Minnesota, 40 km north of Grand Rapids, in the USDA Forest Service Marcell Experimental Forest (MEF). The S1 bog was harvested in successive strip cuts in 1969 and 1974 and the cut areas were allowed to naturally regenerate. The 1974 strips are characterized by medium density of 3-5 meter black spruce and larch trees with an open canopy. The 1969 harvest strips are characterized by a higher density of 3-5 meter black spruce and larch trees with a generally closed canopy.
Survey Grid:
The full S-1 ombrotrophic bog was surveyed through direct measurements of 165 plots distributed on a 20 meter spacing along 30 northwest-to-southeast transects. The lag area of the bog (exterior 15 meters) was deemed inappropriate for the experimental treatments and was avoided in this survey. Table 1 shows the land use/cutting history for transects.

Description of the Sampling Event:
On the 21 and 22 September 2009 ORNL and U.S. Forest Service staff surveyed the areal extent of the S1 Bog for vegetation and peat characteristics.
Vegetation Survey:
Tree species (Picea mariana, Larix laracina, Betula papyrifera, Alnus spp. and Acer rubrum), number, diameter at 1.3 meters (DBH) (Figure 7), and height were evaluated within a 2.5 meter radius of the plot center. Overall area of 19.63 m2for each 5 meter diameter plot.
Seedling/sapling species and count were evaluated within a 1 m radius of the plot center. Overall area of 3.14 m2 for the 2 meter diameter subplot.
A semi-quantitative visual estimation of the cover of the dominant ericaceous shrub cover (Ledum groenlandicum, Chaemedaphne calyculata, Vaccinium spp.) was made within a 1-m subplot.
Notes were taken regarding the condition of the Sphagnum layer, the presence of other common forms of ground vegetation, and the occurrence of buried logs within the peat.
Photographs:
North, east, south, and west photographs from each plot center were also obtained.

Peat Depth Push Probe Measurements:
The thickness of peat in the S1 Bog was measured directly with manual push probes on September 21 and 22, 2009. Multiple push probe measurements were made using 0.5 cm diameter metal rods at the 165 predetermined plot locations. The plots were laid out on a surveyed 20-m grid over the S1 Bog.
Peat depth was obtained by the insertion of steel rods vertically into the peat layer to the point of refusal associated with the peat to mineral soil transition. Multiple measurements were obtained at the center of most plots to evaluate the variability between measurements.
The direct push probe measurements are also reported in Slater et al. (2012), as an integral part of the 3D visualization of peat depth in the S1 Bog. See also Parsekian et al. (2012) for additional analyses.
